Alright, let me think this through. I've been doing this 35 years so I pretty much know the rhythm, but every year's a little different.

I've got 10.1 mu total. I keep about 7 mu in the wheat-maize double crop — that's my bread and butter, feeds the family and brings in steady grain money. The other 3.1 mu I put in cotton. Cotton's more work and the price bounces around, but it's been in that western plot for years and the soil does alright with it. Rotating it with grain would mean redoing everything and I'm not chasing that at 55.

**Wheat (the 7 mu):**
I'll plant around October 10-15, same window I always use. I'll buy certified seed from the agri-supply shop — Jimai or Shixin variety, whatever they have fresh. Cost's about 8 yuan per jin, maybe 40 yuan/mu for seed. Before planting I put down about 40 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu as base. That gives me roughly 6 kg N, 6 P, 6 K to start. Then at jointing in March I topdress urea — about 25 kg/mu, so another 11-12 kg N. Total N around 17-18 kg/mu, which is what I've settled on over the years. Any more and it lodges; any less and the ears are thin.

Irrigation: winter watering in December if the ground's dry, then jointing water in March, heading in April, and one more at grain fill if May is dry. So 3-4 times. Pumping costs me maybe 25 yuan/mu per time with the diesel well. I'll spray herbicide once in spring for weeds, and if I see aphids at heading I'll do insecticide — usually do. Yield I'm looking for 450 kg/mu. Last year I got 470, year before 420 — depends on the spring rain.

**Maize (same 7 mu after wheat):**
This is the tight one. Wheat comes off around June 10, I need maize in the ground within a week or the season runs out. I hire the combine for wheat harvest (60 yuan/mu) and use the no-till planter behind it — 30 yuan/mu for that. Zhengdan or Xianyu hybrid seed, around 50 yuan/mu.

Fertilizer: I put about 35 kg of compound (slow-release 26-10-12 or similar) at planting, no topdress most years because it's hard to get back in there when the maize is tall. So roughly 9 kg N base, and I'll side-dress 15 kg urea at V8 if the plants look pale — another 7 kg N. Call it 15-16 kg N total. Irrigation once or twice in July-August if the summer rains don't come. Herbicide right after planting, one insecticide for armyworm if I see damage. Yield target 500 kg/mu.

**Cotton (3.1 mu):**
Plant late April under film — I'll buy the film and lay it myself, wife helps. Seed about 60 yuan/mu for a Bt variety. Base fertilizer 30 kg compound per mu, then topdress urea 20 kg at bud stage and maybe another 10 kg at flowering. So 13-14 kg N total. I do 2 irrigations usually — once at budding, once at boll fill. 

Cotton is the labor-heavy one. Picking takes forever and my wife and I can't do 3 mu alone at 55. I'll hire 2-3 neighbors for maybe 8-10 days total during the pickings in September-October. 100 yuan/day per person. Pesticide on cotton I spray 3-4 times — bollworm, aphids, mites. That's just how cotton is.

Yield 250 kg/mu lint is what I plan for. Price is the worry — if it drops below 6 yuan/jin I barely break even after labor.

**Overall:** Money's tight with just the two of us and the kids working in town. I don't have cash to experiment. I stick with what's worked. The fertilizer rates I use are a bit above what the extension fellow recommends, but I've learned the hard way that underfeeding wheat in a dry spring costs more than the extra bag of urea.
